# Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin — facts

> Source-anchored units about Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin: 33 across 15 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 33 units · 15 sources · rights: quote -->

## Definitions

- [statement] Hyperliquid's docs say cross margin is the default and isolated margin is also supported, which constrains an asset's collateral to that asset. A liquidation of an isolated position does not affect cross positions, and a cross liquidation does not affect isolated positions. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations

## How it works

- [statement] Hyperliquid backstop liquidation differs by mode. In cross mode, all cross positions and cross margin transfer to the liquidator. In isolated mode, only that isolated position and its isolated margin transfer, and the user's cross margin and positions are untouched. The trigger is account equity below 2/3 of maintenance margin after the order-book attempt fails. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://thogiti.github.io/2025/03/27/Anatomy-DEX-Exploit-Hyperliquid-Perp-JELLY.html
- [statement] Drift perp markets can carry separate high-leverage-mode initial and maintenance ratios, selected when the user has high-leverage mode enabled. In that mode the program uses the high-leverage maintenance ratio, but the ordinary initial ratio for size-adjustment. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/state/perp_market.rs · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] FTI Consulting argues unified (cross-asset) margin is efficient in calm markets because profits offset losses, but under stress it ties portfolios to their weakest assets. It notes a large share of exposure before the 10 October 2025 crash sat on unified-margin venues, and that long-only collateral sell-offs may not be offset by short profits. (low confidence) — https://www.fticonsulting.com/insights/articles/crypto-crash-october-2025-leverage-met-liquidity · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] Hyperliquid's backstop liquidation reaches only the margin pool of the failing mode. It applies when equity falls below 2/3 of maintenance margin and order-book liquidation has not restored the account. A cross backstop liquidation transfers all the trader's cross positions and cross margin to the liquidator vault, which leaves zero equity if the trader has no isolated positions. An isolated backstop liquidation transfers only that position and its isolated margin, and leaves cross margin and positions untouched. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://thogiti.github.io/2025/03/27/Anatomy-DEX-Exploit-Hyperliquid-Perp-JELLY.html
- [statement] Hyperliquid's docs say a cross position's liquidation price does not depend on the leverage setting, because lower leverage only locks more collateral. An isolated position's liquidation price does depend on leverage, because the isolated margin allocated equals the initial margin set. The documented formula is liq_price = price - side * margin_available / position_size / (1 - l * side), with l = 1 / MAINTENANCE_LEVERAGE and side = 1 for longs and -1 for shorts. margin_available is account_value - maintenance_margin_required for cross and isolated_margin - maintenance_margin_required for isolated. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] Flash Trade's docs do not name a margin mode. They describe collateral position by position: shorts always post USDC, and each long market has a fixed backing asset in its pool (SOL longs use JitoSOL, BNB and XRP longs use BTC, equities use SPY). The user can pay with another balance, and the protocol swaps it into the backing asset for a pool swap fee. Flash says it needs no insurance fund because the pool is always the counterparty. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-03) — https://docs.flash.trade/flash-trade/flash-trade-protocol/perpetuals-specifications/collateral-specification.md · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.flash.trade/flash-trade/flash-trade-protocol/perpetuals-specifications/liquidation.md
- [statement] Hyperliquid says a cross position's actual liquidation price does not depend on its leverage setting, because lower leverage only locks more collateral. An isolated position's liquidation price does depend on leverage, because the isolated margin allocated equals the initial margin set. Funding payments and unrealized PnL on other cross positions can still move a cross liquidation price after the position opens. (low confidence) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] On Hyperliquid, the margin mode sets how much a backstop liquidation takes. Backstop liquidation applies when equity falls below two thirds of maintenance margin and order-book liquidation has not restored the account. A cross backstop liquidation transfers all of the trader's cross positions and cross margin to the liquidator vault, which leaves zero equity if the trader holds no isolated position. An isolated backstop liquidation transfers only that position and its isolated margin. The maintenance margin is not returned to the trader in either case. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://thogiti.github.io/2025/03/27/Anatomy-DEX-Exploit-Hyperliquid-Perp-JELLY.html
- [statement] Isolation does not shield a trader's counterparties. Hyperliquid's auto-deleveraging rule covers isolated positions: when a user's account value or an isolated position value turns negative, traders on the opposite side are ranked by unrealized PnL and leverage, and their positions close at the previous mark price against the underwater user. OtterSec's reverse engineering reports that strict-isolated assets skip the aggregate-shortfall gate and go straight into the ADL queue. That finding rests on testnet state, and the author says mainnet metadata is hard to verify. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/auto-deleveraging · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://osec.io/blog/2026-06-22-hyperliquid-risk-engine

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] On Hyperliquid, the margin to open a position is position_size * mark_price / leverage, with leverage an integer up to the asset's max and checked only on opening. Maintenance margin is half of the initial margin at max leverage, and max leverage varies from 3x to 40x by asset. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations
- [statement] Hyperliquid sets maintenance margin at half of the initial margin at the asset's max leverage. That gives 1.25% for 40x assets and 16.7% for 3x assets. A cross position is liquidated when account value, including unrealized PnL, falls below maintenance margin times total open notional. An isolated position follows the same rule using only its own isolated margin and its own notional. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining
- [statement] Cross margin does not count a dollar of deposit as a dollar of margin. Velocity applies an asset weight below 1 to each non-quote deposit, with separate initial and maintenance weights. The initial weight shrinks once a market's total deposits pass a scale-start threshold, and an IMF factor lowers weights further for large holdings. Negative unsettled perp PnL always counts in full. Positive unsettled PnL is weighted by per-market weights that start at 0 for initial margin and 100% for maintenance. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/margin · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/state/perp_market.rs
- [statement] Velocity measures distance to liquidation as health = 100 * (1 - maintenance margin requirement / total collateral), using maintenance-weighted collateral. An account becomes liquidatable at health 0. Liquidation starts partial and aims for the maintenance requirement plus a 2% buffer. In the program, MarginContext carries a margin_buffer, and cross and isolated calculations have separate exit checks (can_exit_cross_margin_liquidation and can_exit_isolated_margin_liquidation). (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/account-health · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/state/margin_calculation.rs
- [statement] Accrued fees move the liquidation price toward the market even when the price is flat. Jupiter's formula subtracts close_fee and the accumulated borrow_fee from collateral before comparing with size / max_lev. If fees exceed collateral_size - size / max_lev, the liquidation price passes the entry price. Jupiter says the effect is largest above 10x leverage. Flash Trade likewise lists unsettled obligations, the close fee plus accrued margin fees, as a liquidation-price input that moves it without price action. (high confidence) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.flash.trade/flash-trade/flash-trade-protocol/perpetuals-specifications/liquidation.md
- [statement] Zeta Markets' landing page says it offered up to 20x leverage with cross margin and has ceased operating as of May 2025, naming Bullet as its successor. The page gives no initial or maintenance margin ratios. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.zeta.markets/ · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] Hyperliquid computes initial margin as position_size * mark_price / leverage. The user picks an integer leverage from 1 to the asset's maximum, and the exchange checks leverage only when a position opens. Maintenance margin is half of the initial margin at max leverage, which is 1.25% for a 40x asset and 16.7% for a 3x asset. A cross position is liquidated when account value, including unrealized PnL, falls below maintenance margin times total open notional. An isolated position uses the same test with only its own margin and notional. OtterSec's reverse engineering of the node binary also finds separate code paths: cross margin runs an account-wide check, while isolated equity is the position's isolated margin plus its own PnL. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations, https://osec.io/blog/2026-06-22-hyperliquid-risk-engine
- [statement] Drift and Velocity set initial and maintenance margin ratios per perp market, and an admin can change them. Velocity says maximum leverage is the reciprocal of the initial ratio, and that the program bounds the ratio between 1.25% (80x) and 100% (1x). An IMF factor raises the required ratio as a position grows: for ordinary users, get_margin_ratio returns the larger of the base ratio and a size-adjusted ratio. A market can also carry separate high-leverage-mode initial and maintenance ratios, which apply to users in high leverage mode. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/margin · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/state/perp_market.rs
- [statement] Accrued fees move a liquidation price toward the market even when the price is flat. Jupiter's formula subtracts close_fee and the accumulated borrow_fee from collateral before comparing with size / max_lev. If fees exceed collateral_size - size / max_lev, the liquidation price passes the entry price and the position can be liquidated without an adverse price move. Jupiter says the effect is largest above 10x and on long holds, and that withdrawing collateral raises leverage and moves the liquidation price toward the market. Flash Trade's docs describe the same drift from unsettled close and margin fees. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/positions-and-collateral, https://docs.flash.trade/flash-trade/flash-trade-protocol/perpetuals-specifications/liquidation.md
- [statement] Cross-asset (unified) margin ties account health to collateral prices, so a bad price for collateral can push accounts through maintenance. During the 10 October 2025 crash, USDe traded in the mid-$0.60s on Binance while it stayed near $1 elsewhere. FTI says margin systems that priced collateral from the venue's own spot market marked it down sharply and pushed thousands of accounts through maintenance thresholds. CoinShares says Binance confirmed it priced from internal spot markets, and that BNSOL and WBETH also lost their pegs. Cointelegraph reports the USDe dislocation was later attributed to a platform-specific internal oracle issue. (high confidence) — https://www.fticonsulting.com/insights/articles/crypto-crash-october-2025-leverage-met-liquidity · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://coinshares.com/it/insights/knowledge/billions-in-liquidations-what-happened, https://cointelegraph.com/news/cz-denies-binance-role-october-crypto-liquidation-usde-depeg
- [statement] Hyperliquid limits margin removal. Unrealized PnL can leave an isolated position or the cross account only if the remaining margin is at least 10% of total position value and still meets initial margin: transfer_margin_required = max(initial_margin_required, 0.1 * total_position_value). The rule covers withdrawals, transfers to the spot wallet and isolated margin removal. A community wiki repeats the formula. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://hyperliquid-co.gitbook.io/wiki/architecture/hypercore/dex/clearinghouse/margin-management

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Hyperliquid withdrawal or transfer of unrealized PnL from an isolated position or the cross account is limited by transfer_margin_required = max(initial_margin_required, 0.1 * total_position_value). Some assets are 'strict isolated', which adds a constraint that isolated margin cannot be removed. HIP-3 DEXs also support a 'no cross' mode. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] On Hyperliquid, the margin needed to open a position is position_size * mark_price / leverage. The user picks an integer leverage from 1 up to the asset's maximum. The exchange checks leverage only when the position opens, so the user must monitor it afterwards. Initial margin on a cross position cannot be withdrawn. Isolated margin can be added or removed after opening, and an isolated position applies its own unrealized PnL as extra margin to itself. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.trade.xyz/risk-and-margining/margin-modes
- [statement] Which positions share cross margin on Hyperliquid depends on the account abstraction. Under a unified account or portfolio margin, cross positions in HIP-3 DEXs that use the same collateral share margin. Under the standard abstraction, cross margin applies to each DEX separately. HIP-3 DEXs can also offer a 'no cross' mode that allows isolated margin with margin removal but no cross margin. Some assets are 'strict isolated': margin cannot be removed and is released in proportion as the position closes. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/account-abstraction-modes, https://docs.trade.xyz/risk-and-margining/margin-modes
- [statement] Hyperliquid defaults to cross margin and also offers isolated margin. Some assets are strict isolated: margin cannot be removed and is released in proportion as the position closes. HIP-3 DEXs can offer a no-cross mode that allows isolated margin with margin removal. Which positions share cross margin depends on the account abstraction. Unified accounts and portfolio margin share cross margin across DEXs that use the same collateral. Standard accounts cross-margin each DEX separately. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/margining · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/account-abstraction-modes
- [statement] Jupiter Perps keeps collateral on each position in its JLP markets (SOL, ETH, wBTC). A long posts the traded asset and a short posts USDC, and the collateral token cannot change after opening. A user can hold at most six positions, one per asset and side. A second order on the same asset and side merges into the first: sizes and collaterals add, so combined leverage is total size over total collateral. Jupiter's JLP-market pages never use the words cross or isolated. Jupiter does not issue margin calls. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/positions-and-collateral · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/beta-markets
- [statement] On Jupiter's Beta markets, a position is liquidated when the mark price reaches its liquidation price, one tier slice at a time, and the collateral left after the loss and fees returns to the trader. In a fast market that can be little or nothing. On the JLP markets, all remaining collateral is taken as a liquidation fee instead. Beta withdrawals are capped below free collateral, and unrealized profit cannot be withdrawn until the position closes. The docs say there is no auto-deleveraging on Beta markets at launch. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-28) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/beta-markets · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/liquidation
- [statement] Solflare Perps launched with isolated margin only. Each position has its own collateral, a liquidation puts only that position's collateral at risk, and cross margin is not available at launch. Solflare says the product runs on the Phoenix protocol and that users sign orders directly with Phoenix. Default leverage for first-time traders is 2x. Solflare warns that isolated margin limits but does not eliminate loss: the position's own collateral can be lost in full. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-24) — https://help.solflare.com/en/articles/16198228-understanding-leverage-isolated-margin · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://help.solflare.com/en/articles/16201693-risks-associated-with-perps-trading
- [statement] Velocity measures distance to liquidation as health = 100 * (1 - maintenance margin requirement / total collateral), using maintenance-weighted collateral. The account is liquidatable at health 0. The Initial view uses stricter weights and gates new risk, so free collateral can look usable on the Maintenance view while the Initial check rejects a new position. Positive unsettled P&L is weighted per market, starting at 0 for initial margin and 100% for maintenance, and a $100 per-position ceiling limits how much of it counts toward initial margin. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/protocol/trading/margin/account-health · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/margin

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Drift's on-chain program distinguishes three margin requirement types: Initial, Fill and Maintenance. Fill is the average of the market's initial and maintenance margin ratios. Drift's docs likewise say fill checks use the midpoint of the scaled initial and maintenance weights. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://github.com/drift-labs/protocol-v2/blob/master/programs/drift/src/state/perp_market.rs · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/margin
- [statement] Jupiter Perps documents per-position collateral and does not describe cross-margin. Shorts always use USDC collateral and a second same-asset, same-side position merges into one with sizes and collateral added. Jupiter does not prompt for more collateral before liquidation, and withdrawing collateral raises leverage and moves the liquidation price closer. The page states no maintenance margin ratio. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.jup.ag/user-docs/trade/perps/positions-and-collateral · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] Solflare Perps launched with isolated margin only. Each position has its own collateral, so liquidation risks only that position's collateral, and cross margin was stated as not available at launch. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-24) — https://help.solflare.com/en/articles/16198228-understanding-leverage-isolated-margin · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin
- [statement] In cross margin, a deposit other than the quote asset counts at less than its market value. Velocity applies separate initial and maintenance asset weights below 1, and borrows carry liability weights above 1. The initial weight shrinks once a spot market's total deposits pass a scale-start threshold. An IMF factor lowers weights for large holdings: weight = min(base weight, 1.1 / (1 + sqrt(size) * imf factor)). Neodyme's audit describes the same weighting for Drift, where a requirement is met only if weighted assets are at least weighted liabilities. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://docs.velocity.exchange/trading/margin · keywords: Cross versus isolated margin and initial and maintenance margin · also: https://neodyme.io/reports/Drift.pdf
